title: Why Your AI UX Is Broken (and It's Not the Model's Fault) — Mike Christensen, Ably

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's core concept of durable sessions—persistent, shared, stateful media that survive connection failures and enable auto-resume—directly matches durable execution runtimes that make agent work survive failure. The durable session pattern is cross-domain, demonstrated via a support chat demo but applicable to any AI application, and Ably provides a developer platform other teams build on. The talk addresses architecture design of durable sessions and production reliability concerns including disconnect recovery, resumability, and multi-agent coordination without centralized orchestration. Requires familiarity with SSE, WebSockets, and pub/sub concepts but remains accessible to engineers building AI chat applications. Conference presentation with live demos showing multi-tab sync, forced disconnect recovery, concurrent agents, and human agent handoff. All evidence anchors are directly quoted from the transcript with grade said_in_transcript.

summary: The talk opens with Mike Christensen noting that nearly everyone has built AI chat apps using the default pattern: direct HTTP streaming via SSE, where a single client establishes a single connection to a single agent. While easy to prototype, this paradigm couples stream health to one connection. Christensen shares findings from Ably's conversations with 40+ companies across 10 industries, identifying three foundational capabilities: resilient delivery, continuity across surfaces, and live control. With direct HTTP streaming, the stream's health is tied to the client's connection—if it drops, the stream is gone. The connection is private, so other tabs or devices have no visibility, and other clients can't steer the agent. SSE is one-way, making abort and resume mutually exclusive; Vercel's AI SDK docs confirm this. Even WebSockets don't solve multi-device visibility. Durable sessions address this by acting as a persistent, stateful, shared medium between agent and client layers. For concurrent multi-agent architectures, the orchestrator pattern forces a dual-purpose role—delegating tasks while proxying granular updates—adding unnecessary complexity. Durable sessions let all agents write independently to the session, and clients subscribe to a single entity for full visibility. This pattern maps to pub/sub: Ably channels are independently addressable, persistent (messages outlive any connection/device/agent), and fully resumable. Ably has introduced the AI Transport SDK, a drop-in layer that plugs into any event stream format and handles durable sessions via Ably channels with automatic event materialization, resumability, multiplexing, and multi-client fanout with bidirectional control. It also includes push notifications and shared data objects. The live demo shows multi-tab sync, page refresh with auto-recovery, forced network disconnect with self-recovery, concurrent agents working simultaneously, canceling from a different tab, and a handoff to a human support agent who joins mid-conversation with full interaction history visible.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction to AI chat applications
sections.summary: Christensen opens by asking the audience who has built AI chat apps—nearly everyone has. The fundamental building block is a user sending a message to an agent on the back end, with the agent streaming a response back live.

sections.title: Current implementation: Direct HTTP streaming and SSE
sections.summary: The default pattern in popular frameworks (Vercel AI SDK, LangChain) is SSE-based direct HTTP streaming: the client makes a request, establishes a persistent point-to-point connection, and the agent pipes LLM events back. This is easy to prototype but fundamentally oriented around a single client-to-single agent connection. Christensen introduces himself as a staff engineer at Ably, a real-time messaging platform at massive scale.

sections.title: Three foundational capabilities for great AI products
sections.summary: Based on conversations with 40+ companies across 10 industries, three capabilities separate fragile demos from great products: resilient delivery (streams surviving disconnections), continuity across surfaces (sessions following users across tabs and devices), and live control (communicating with agents mid-task, as in Claude Code).

sections.title: Limitations of direct HTTP streaming
sections.summary: The root cause is coupling to a single request. Stream health is tied to the client's connection—if it drops, the stream is gone. The connection is a private pipe, so other tabs or devices have no visibility. Since the stream isn't shared, other clients can't reach the agent to steer or interrupt it.

sections.title: Introducing durable sessions
sections.summary: A pattern companies are adopting: decouple the agent layer from the client layer using durable sessions—a persistent, stateful, shared medium between agents and clients—making resilient streaming, multi-tab/device experiences, and live agent interaction much easier to build.

sections.title: Resumability in streams
sections.summary: With direct HTTP streaming, when a connection drops mid-stream, the LLM keeps generating events with nowhere to go. Building resume requires storing events in Redis with sequence numbers and implementing an explicit resume handler—all custom plumbing. Durable sessions solve this by letting agents write to the session and clients resume from it independently.

sections.title: The conflict between SSE, resumability, and live control
sections.summary: SSE is strictly one-way: a stop button requires signaling cancel, but the only client signal is closing the connection, indistinguishable from a disconnect. The agent can't tell cancel from disconnect, so resume and cancel are mutually exclusive. Vercel's AI SDK docs confirm abort is incompatible with resume. WebSockets offer bidirectional control but don't solve everything.

sections.title: Multi-device and multi-tab synchronization issues
sections.summary: Even with WebSockets, a second tab has no visibility of the in-progress stream. Switching to a phone provides no visibility and no upstream channel. Durable sessions fix this: all clients hold persistent connections to the shared session with constant visibility and can route to any agent from any surface.

sections.title: Handling concurrent multi-agent architectures
sections.summary: In orchestrator-based multi-agent architectures, the orchestrator is forced into a dual-purpose role: delegating tasks to sub-agents while also proxying granular progress updates back to the client. This adds unnecessary complexity since the orchestrator only cares about final results. Durable sessions solve this by letting all agents write independently to the session layer, so granular updates don't flow through a central orchestrator. Clients subscribe to a single entity—the session—for full visibility of all agent and client activity, drastically simplifying the architecture.

sections.title: Using Pub/Sub and Ably channels for durable sessions
sections.summary: The durable session pattern resembles pub/sub. Ably channels provide the needed properties: independently addressable (any client or agent connects by specifying a channel name), persistent (messages outlive any individual connection, device, or agent), and fully resumable (dropped connections automatically reconnect and resume from exactly where they left off). Many Ably customers have built resilient multi-surface experiences this way.

sections.title: Introducing Ably AI Transport SDK
sections.summary: Ably AI Transport is a drop-in SDK that automatically plugs into any event stream format from any model provider or agent framework. Under the hood it uses Ably channels for the durable session layer, handling materialization (streaming text chunks into complete responses), automatic resumability, multiplexing of concurrent activity, and multi-client/multi-device fanout with bidirectional control. It also includes push notifications for background async work and APIs for shared subscribable data objects for real-time collaboration.

sections.title: Live demo of durable session capabilities
sections.summary: The demo shows an AI support chat for an electronics shop. Features include client-side and server-side tool calls (location lookup, store list) that work across multiple tabs out of the box via the durable session layer. Refreshing the page during a streamed response keeps everything in sync automatically with no additional agent logic. Forcing a network disconnect and reconnect lets everything carry on automatically. The demo shows a specialized product research sub-agent kicked off from a second tab with granular visibility, then canceled from the first tab—demonstrating cross-client cancel. Two agents work concurrently (purchasing headphones and canceling an existing order) in the same session, fully synchronized without centralized coordination.

sections.title: Handoff to human support agent
sections.summary: The user, unhappy with a refund price, requests a human agent. A support agent view is opened and the human agent joins the session mid-conversation with full visibility of all prior interaction history between the customer and the AI agent. The human can then send messages as a participant in the same session. Christensen closes and thanks the audience.
